bento.reader_kicker: Read the Act like a story

reader.title: Consent
reader.says: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous - given by a clear affirmative action.
reader.plain: People must actually say yes. Pre-ticked boxes and buried clauses don't count.

reader.title: Children's data
reader.says: Verifiable parental consent is required, and tracking or targeted advertising directed at children is barred.
reader.plain: Under-18s get extra protection: get a parent's okay, and never profile kids.

reader.title: Security safeguards
reader.says: A Data Fiduciary must keep personal data accurate, protect it with reasonable safeguards, and report breaches.
reader.plain: Guard the data you hold - and own up fast if something goes wrong.

reader.title: Right to access
reader.says: A Data Principal may obtain a summary of their personal data and the identities it has been shared with.
reader.plain: People can ask what you hold on them, and exactly who you shared it with.

reader.title: Notice
reader.says: A notice must describe the personal data sought and the purpose for which it will be processed.
reader.plain: Tell people what you're collecting and why - before you collect it.

risk.heading: Can your organization answer these 7 questions?
risk.subheading: One question for each stage of our 7D DPDP framework - Discover to Drive. Mark each and your readiness score updates live.
questions: Discover - Do you have a complete, current inventory of every personal-data flow across cloud, on-premise, vendors, and AI tools?
Define - Can you show a documented purpose, lawful basis, and retention period for each category of personal data you process?
Design - Are your privacy notices, consent capture, and consent-withdrawal flows DPDP-ready and in clear, plain language?
Defend - If a breach happened today, could you contain it and notify the Board and affected people within 72 hours?
Deploy - Have DPDP processes, role-based training, and signed vendor DPAs actually rolled out across every department?
Demonstrate - Could you hand an auditor or the Data Protection Board evidence of your compliance on demand?
Drive - Does someone own DPDP day-to-day, with regular Data Principal rights, grievance, and AI-privacy reviews?

about.title: About TrustStack
about.body: TrustStack is a clear, modern home for India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules 2025. We translate dense legal text into plain meaning, cross-linked to penalties, templates and case law, so that citizens, students and organisations across India can understand and act on their data-protection rights and duties. Built for awareness in the public interest - not legal advice.
